The clip's structure includes two main components: a first section (420) and a second section (430), which are joined together via a hinge (401). # Clip Assembly for Bracelet and/or Necklace Applications

## Overview

The present disclosure relates to a clip mechanism designed for use with bracelets and/or necklaces. The clip is configured such that, when placed in a closed position, it defines a through hole extending through the body of the clip. This through hole is dimensioned to receive and encircle an elongated member, such as a chain, cord, or band, thereby enabling the clip to be securely mounted onto the jewelry item while maintaining the ability to slide or be positioned along the length of the elongated member as needed.

## Structural Configuration

The clip comprises two primary structural components: a first part and a second part. These two parts are joined together by means of a hinge, which serves as the pivotal connection point between them. This hinge-based connection allows the clip to transition between an open configuration, in which the elongated member can be inserted or removed, and a closed configuration, in which the through hole is fully formed and the elongated member is enclosed within it.

## Resilient Gripping Element

To ensure secure attachment to the elongated member once the clip is closed, a first resilient element is incorporated into the design and positioned within the second part of the clip. This resilient element is provided with a first gripping surface, which is specifically engineered to establish frictional contact with the outer surface of the elongated member. This frictional engagement serves to prevent unwanted sliding or displacement of the clip along the elongated member, thereby maintaining the clip's position once it has been set by the user.

## Cavity and Resilient Element Housing

The second part of the clip is constructed with a radially extending cavity, which serves as the housing for a portion of the first resilient element. Specifically, this cavity accommodates a first resilient part of the element, securing it internally within the structure of the second part. A second resilient part of the same element extends outward from this cavity, protruding into the through hole formed by the closed clip. This configuration allows the second resilient part—bearing the first gripping surface—to make direct contact with the elongated member positioned within the through hole.

## Retention Mechanism

The radially extending cavity is specifically shaped and configured to perform a retention function, ensuring that the first resilient element remains securely fixed in place within the second part of the clip. This design consideration prevents displacement or dislodgement of the resilient element during normal use, while still permitting the second resilient part to flex or deform as necessary to accommodate the frictional gripping action against elongated members of varying diameters or surface textures.

# CLIP FOR BRACELETS AND/OR NECKLACES

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates to a clip device, and more particularly to a clip for bracelets and/or necklaces designed to securely grip an elongated member such as a cord, chain, wire, or string, while allowing for adjustable positioning along the length of said elongated member.

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Clips for bracelets and necklaces are widely used in the jewelry industry to allow wearers to adjust the length of their jewelry items or to add decorative elements that can slide along a cord or chain. Conventional clips often suffer from various drawbacks, including insufficient gripping force, tendency to slip or become dislodged during normal wear, difficulty in manufacturing due to complex assembly requirements, and inadequate retention of internal gripping components.

Many existing clip designs rely on simple mechanical pressure from rigid components pressed against the elongated member, which can result in inconsistent grip strength and potential damage to the surface of the elongated member over time. Additionally, some designs suffer from the internal gripping elements becoming dislodged or shifting position during use, thereby compromising the clip's functionality and reliability.

There exists a need in the art for an improved clip design that provides secure, consistent gripping force while maintaining structural integrity of the internal components, and which can be manufactured efficiently while providing reliable performance over extended periods of use.

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention addresses the aforementioned needs by providing a clip for bracelets and/or necklaces comprising a first part and a second part that are hingedly connected to one another. When the first part and second part are brought together in a closed configuration, they cooperatively define a through hole dimensioned to wreathe (encircle) an elongated member, such as a cord, chain, or similar item used in jewelry construction.

The second part of the clip includes a radial cavity formed therein, within which a resilient element is positioned. This resilient element is specifically configured to frictionally engage and grip the outer surface of the elongated member when the clip is in its closed position, thereby securing the clip at a desired location along the length of the elongated member.

A key aspect of the present invention lies in the specific configuration of the resilient element itself. The resilient element comprises two distinct portions: an inner part and an outer part. The inner part of the resilient element is securely anchored or fixed within the radial cavity of the second part, providing a stable base of attachment. The outer part of the resilient element extends outwardly from the inner part into the through hole formed when the clip is closed, such that the outer part makes direct contact with and grips the surface of the elongated member.

This dual-part configuration of the resilient element provides several advantages over conventional clip designs. By securing the inner part within the cavity while allowing the outer part to extend into the through hole, the resilient element achieves a balance between firm anchoring within the clip structure and effective, flexible engagement with the elongated member. This design ensures that the resilient element does not become dislodged, rotated, or displaced during normal use, while simultaneously providing sufficient flexibility and surface contact area to generate reliable frictional grip force against the elongated member.

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### General Structure of the Clip

Referring to the general structure of the clip according to the present invention, the clip comprises two primary components: a first part and a second part, which are connected to one another by a hinge mechanism. This hinge mechanism allows the first part and second part to pivot relative to one another between an open configuration, in which the elongated member may be inserted or removed from the clip, and a closed configuration, in which the elongated member is secured within the clip.

In the closed configuration, the first part and second part cooperate to define a through hole. This through hole is dimensioned and shaped to receive and wreathe the elongated member, such that the elongated member passes through the clip along the axis of the through hole. The through hole may be circular, oval, or of other suitable cross-sectional shape depending on the shape of the elongated member to be received.

The hinge connecting the first part and second part may be formed integrally with the material of the clip, such as through a living hinge construction, or may be formed as a separate pivot mechanism such as a pin-and-barrel hinge arrangement. The specific hinge construction may be selected based on manufacturing considerations, material properties, and desired durability characteristics.

### The Second Part and Radial Cavity

The second part of the clip is formed with a radial cavity, which extends inwardly from an inner surface of the second part that faces the through hole when the clip is in the closed position. This radial cavity is dimensioned to receive and retain the resilient element described herein.

The radial cavity may be formed with a specific geometry designed to complement the shape of the inner part of the resilient element, such that when the inner part is inserted into the cavity, it is securely retained therein through a combination of mechanical interference, adhesive bonding, or other suitable retention mechanisms. The cavity may include features such as undercuts, ridges, or textured surfaces to enhance retention of the resilient element.

### The Resilient Element

The resilient element of the present invention is a critical component that enables the clip to achieve secure, reliable gripping of the elongated member. The resilient element is formed from a material possessing sufficient elasticity and resilience to deform when contacted by the elongated member, while returning to its original shape when such contact is removed, and to provide sustained frictional engagement over repeated use cycles.

Suitable materials for the resilient element may include, without limitation, natural or synthetic rubber, silicone, thermoplastic elastomers, or other polymeric materials known in the art to possess appropriate elastic properties. The specific material selection may be based on factors including desired durability, resistance to environmental degradation, coefficient of friction against typical elongated member materials, and manufacturing considerations.

As previously noted, the resilient element comprises an inner part and an outer part. The inner part is configured to be received within and securely anchored to the radial cavity formed in the second part of the clip. This anchoring may be achieved through various means, including but not limited to:

1. A press-fit or interference fit between the inner part and the walls of the radial cavity;
2. An adhesive bond between the inner part and the surfaces of the radial cavity;
3. A mechanical interlocking feature, such as a protrusion on the inner part that engages a corresponding recess in the cavity, or vice versa;
4. Overmolding of the inner part directly within the cavity during a manufacturing process, such that the inner part is formed in situ within the second part.

The outer part of the resilient element extends from the inner part in a direction toward the through hole, such that when the clip is in the closed configuration, the outer part projects into the through hole and is positioned to make contact with the outer surface of the elongated member received therein.

The outer part may be shaped to maximize surface contact with the elongated member, such as through a curved or contoured surface that generally conforms to the expected curvature of the elongated member. Alternatively, the outer part may include a plurality of protrusions, ridges, or other surface features designed to enhance frictional engagement with the elongated member.

The dimensional relationship between the inner part and outer part of the resilient element may be varied depending on the specific application and desired performance characteristics. For example, the inner part may be dimensioned to occupy substantially the entire volume of the radial cavity, providing maximum surface area for anchoring, while the outer part may be dimensioned to extend a relatively short distance into the through hole, sufficient to achieve desired frictional contact without excessively restricting the through hole diameter.

### Operation of the Clip

In operation, a user opens the clip by pivoting the first part and second part relative to one another about the hinge, thereby increasing the accessible opening for insertion of the elongated member. The elongated member is then positioned adjacent to the second part such that it will be received within the space that will become the through hole upon closing of the clip.

The user then pivots the first part and second part toward one another, moving the clip into the closed configuration. As the clip closes, the first part and second part cooperate to define the through hole, with the elongated member being received therein. Simultaneously, the outer part of the resilient element, positioned within the through hole, comes into contact with the outer surface of the elongated member.

Due to the resilient nature of the material forming the resilient element, the outer part deforms slightly upon contact with the elongated member, conforming to some degree to the surface contour of the elongated member and generating a frictional grip force therewith. This frictional grip force secures the clip at the desired position along the length of the elongated member, preventing unwanted sliding or displacement of the clip during normal use and wear.

Because the inner part of the resilient element remains securely anchored within the radial cavity of the second part throughout this process, the resilient element as a whole remains properly positioned within the clip structure, ensuring consistent and reliable performance of the frictional gripping function over repeated open-close cycles and extended periods of use.

### Alternative Embodiments

It should be understood that various modifications and alternative embodiments of the present invention are contemplated. For example, in certain embodiments, the first part of the clip may also include a radial cavity and associated resilient element, similar in construction to that described with respect to the second part, such that the elongated member is gripped from multiple directions when the clip is closed.

In other embodiments, the shape and dimensions of the through hole may be varied to accommodate elongated members of different sizes and cross-sectional shapes, including but not limited to circular cords, flat ribbons, chains comprising individual links, or wire-based elongated members.

The hinge mechanism connecting the first part and second part may further include a locking feature configured to releasably retain the clip in the closed configuration, such as a latch, snap-fit engagement, or other suitable locking mechanism, thereby preventing inadvertent opening of the clip during use.

Additionally, the exterior surfaces of the first part and second part may be decorated, textured, or otherwise treated to provide an aesthetically pleasing appearance suitable for use in jewelry applications, including but not limited to plating with precious metals, application of gemstones or other decorative elements, or texturing to simulate various material appearances.

## CONCLUSION

The clip for bracelets and/or necklaces disclosed herein provides a significant improvement over conventional clip designs by providing a resilient element configuration that ensures both secure anchoring within the clip structure and reliable frictional engagement with an elongated member. This dual-function design, achieved through the inner part and outer part configuration of the resilient element, results in a clip that is durable, reliable, and effective for use in jewelry applications requiring adjustable or securable positioning along a cord, chain, or similar elongated member.

# PATENT DISCLOSURE

## HINGED CLIP MECHANISM FOR SECURING BRACELETS AND NECKLACES

---

### FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present disclosure relates generally to jewelry fasteners, and more particularly to a hinged clip mechanism configured to securely and reversibly join opposing ends of a bracelet, necklace, or similar wearable article, incorporating a primary locking mechanism and a redundant safety latch to prevent inadvertent release.

---

### BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional jewelry clasps—such as spring-ring clasps, lobster-claw clasps, and toggle clasps—suffer from several recurring problems. Spring-ring clasps require significant dexterity and often cannot be operated single-handedly. Lobster-claw clasps, while easier to manipulate, rely on small spring-loaded levers that are prone to metal fatigue and unintentional disengagement. Toggle clasps, though easy to open, provide comparatively weak retention and can separate under lateral tension.

There exists a need for a clasp mechanism that combines ease of one-handed operation with a high degree of security against accidental opening, while remaining compact, low-profile, and suitable for a variety of jewelry forms.

---

### SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The disclosed hinged clip mechanism (10) comprises a first body member (12) and a second body member (14) joined along a common hinge axis (16) by cooperating hinge knuckles (18, 20). The second body member (14) houses a spring-biased locking lever (22) that engages a catch recess (44) formed in the first body member (12) when the clip is closed, thereby securing the two halves together. A release button (28), accessible from the exterior of the second body member (14), permits the user to disengage the locking lever (22) and open the clip.

To further reduce the risk of accidental opening, a secondary safety latch (30), independently biased by a small spring (42), overlays the release button (28) and must be manually displaced before the release button (28) can be depressed. Attachment loops (32, 34) are integrally formed on the first and second body members (12, 14), respectively, and are configured to receive the terminal ends (36, 38) of a bracelet or necklace chain, such as via jump rings or crimped fittings.

---

### BRIEF DESCRIPTION OF THE DRAWINGS

**FIG. 1** – Perspective view of the hinged clip mechanism (10) in the closed and locked configuration.

**FIG. 2** – Exploded perspective view showing the first body member (12), second body member (14), hinge pin (16), locking lever (22), spring element (24), and safety latch (30).

**FIG. 3** – Cross-sectional side view through the hinge axis (40), illustrating engagement of the locking lever (22) within the catch recess (44).

**FIG. 4** – Detail view of the release button (28) and safety latch (30) in the disengaged (unlocked) position.

**FIG. 5** – Perspective view of the clip mechanism (10) in the open configuration, with the first body member (12) pivoted away from the second body member (14) about the hinge pin (16).

---

### DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENT

Referring to the drawings, the hinged clip mechanism (10) generally comprises the following numbered elements:

| Ref. No. | Element |
|----------|---------|
| 10 | Hinged clip mechanism (overall assembly) |
| 12 | First body member |
| 14 | Second body member |
| 16 | Hinge pin |
| 18 | First hinge knuckle (formed on element 12) |
| 20 | Second hinge knuckle (formed on element 14) |
| 22 | Locking lever (tongue) |
| 24 | Primary biasing spring (for locking lever 22) |
| 26 | Catch tip of locking lever 22 |
| 28 | Release button / actuator |
| 30 | Safety latch |
| 32 | First attachment loop (on element 12) |
| 34 | Second attachment loop (on element 14) |
| 36 | First jewelry chain terminal end |
| 38 | Second jewelry chain terminal end |
| 40 | Hinge axis |
| 42 | Secondary biasing spring (for safety latch 30) |
| 44 | Catch recess (formed in element 12) |
| 46 | User-actuated grip tab (on safety latch 30) |

**Hinge Assembly.** The first body member (12) and second body member (14) are joined at a common hinge axis (40) via interlocking hinge knuckles (18, 20), through which a hinge pin (16) is inserted, permitting rotational movement of the first body member (12) relative to the second body member (14) between open and closed positions.

**Locking Mechanism.** The second body member (14) houses a locking lever (22), which is biased toward an engaged position by a primary spring (24). When the first body member (12) is pivoted into the closed position, a catch tip (26) formed at the distal end of the locking lever (22) snaps into a corresponding catch recess (44) formed in the first body member (12), thereby preventing separation of the two body members under normal tension.

**Release Mechanism.** A release button (28) is mounted on the exterior surface of the second body member (14) and is mechanically coupled to the locking lever (22) such that depression of the release button (28) withdraws the catch tip (26) from the catch recess (44), permitting the first body member (12) to be pivoted open about the hinge pin (16).

**Safety Latch.** To prevent unintended actuation of the release button (28)—for example, due to snagging on clothing—a safety latch (30) is slidably or pivotally mounted adjacent to the release button (28) and biased into a blocking position by a secondary spring (42). The safety latch (30) includes a grip tab (46) that a user may manually displace to expose the release button (28), which may then be depressed to disengage the locking lever (22).

**Attachment Loops.** The first body member (12) and second body member (14) each terminate in an attachment loop (32, 34, respectively), configured to receive and retain the terminal ends (36, 38) of a bracelet or necklace chain, such retention being accomplished by conventional jump rings, crimp beads, or soldered connections.

**Operation.** In use, the terminal ends (36, 38) of the jewelry item are joined to the clip mechanism (10) via the attachment loops (32, 34). To close the clip, the first body member (12) is pivoted about the hinge pin (16) toward the second body member (14) until the catch tip (26) of the locking lever (22) engages the catch recess (44), producing an audible and tactile confirmation of closure. To open the clip, the user displaces the safety latch (30) via the grip tab (46), then depresses the release button (28), withdrawing the catch tip (26) from the catch recess (44) and permitting the first body member (12) to be pivoted open.

---

### ALTERNATIVE EMBODIMENTS

It is contemplated that the hinge knuckles (18, 20) may be replaced with a living hinge formed from a resilient polymer or metal alloy, obviating the need for a discrete hinge pin (16). It is further contemplated that the locking lever (22) and safety latch (30) may be combined into a single dual-function component, or that magnetic elements may be incorporated into the first body member (12) and second body member (14) to supplement mechanical retention.

---

### CLAIMS

**1.** A hinged clip mechanism (10) for securing a bracelet or necklace, comprising:
a first body member (12) having a first attachment loop (32);
a second body member (14) having a second attachment loop (34);
a hinge pin (16) rotatably joining the first body member (12) and the second body member (14) along a hinge axis (40);
a locking lever (22) disposed within the second body member (14) and biased by a primary spring (24) toward engagement with a catch recess (44) formed in the first body member (12); and
a release button (28) operatively coupled to the locking lever (22) and configured, upon actuation, to disengage the locking lever (22) from the catch recess (44).

**2.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 1, further comprising a safety latch (30) biased by a secondary spring (42) into a position blocking actuation of the release button (28), the safety latch (30) including a grip tab (46) manually operable to expose the release button (28).

**3.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 1, wherein the first and second attachment loops (32, 34) are configured to receive terminal ends (36, 38) of a jewelry chain via jump rings.

**4.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 1, wherein the hinge pin (16) engages first and second hinge knuckles (18, 20) formed integrally with the first body member (12) and second body member (14), respectively.

**5.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 1, wherein the locking lever (22) terminates in a catch tip (26) shaped to seat within the catch recess (44) with an audible confirmation upon closure.

**6.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 2, wherein the safety latch (30) is slidably mounted relative to the second body member (14).

**7.** The hinged clip mechanism (10) of claim 1, wherein the hinge pin (16) and hinge knuckles (18, 20) are replaced by a living hinge formed of a resilient material.

---

### ABSTRACT

A hinged clip mechanism (10) for securing bracelets or necklaces is disclosed, comprising a first body member (12) and second body member (14) joined by a hinge pin (16), a spring-biased locking lever (22) that engages a catch recess (44) to secure the clip in a closed configuration, a release button (28) for disengaging the locking lever (22), and a redundant safety latch (30) that must be manually displaced prior to actuation of the release button (28), thereby reducing the likelihood of accidental opening while maintaining ease of single-handed operation.

# PATENT APPLICATION EXCERPT

## TITLE OF INVENTION
**JEWELRY CLASP ASSEMBLY WITH HINGED MEMBER, APERTURE, AND RESILIENT RETENTION MECHANISM**

---

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to jewelry fasteners, and more particularly to a clasp assembly for securing jewelry articles such as necklaces, bracelets, and similar ornamental items, incorporating a hinged connection, a through-hole for chain or cord engagement, and a resiliently biased gripping element disposed within an internal cavity to provide secure yet releasable retention.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional jewelry clasps often suffer from inadequate retention force, difficulty of one-handed operation, and mechanical failure due to fatigue of spring components over repeated use. There exists a need in the art for a clasp assembly that combines structural durability with ease of use while maintaining secure engagement between mating jewelry components.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

In accordance with one embodiment, the present invention provides a jewelry clasp assembly comprising:

(a) a first body member and a second body member operatively connected by a **hinge assembly**, said hinge assembly permitting pivotal movement of the second body member relative to the first body member between an open position and a closed position;

(b) at least one **through hole** formed in the first body member, said through hole extending from a first surface to an opposing second surface thereof, and configured to receive a jump ring, chain end, or other jewelry-attachment component therethrough; and

(c) a **cavity** formed within the second body member, said cavity housing a **resilient gripping element** therein, wherein the resilient gripping element is configured to exert a biasing force against a mating engagement surface of the first body member when the clasp assembly is in the closed position, thereby releasably securing the first body member and the second body member together.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE PREFERRED EMBODIMENT

Referring now to the drawings, wherein like reference numerals designate corresponding parts throughout the several views:

### First Body Member and Through Hole

The clasp assembly **10** comprises a first body member **12** having a proximal end **14** and a distal end **16**. Formed within the first body member **12** is a through hole **18**, extending transversely through the thickness of the first body member **12** from a first surface **20** to a second surface **22**. The through hole **18** is dimensioned to receive a connector element, such as a split ring or soldered jump ring, enabling attachment of the clasp assembly **10** to a length of chain, cord, or other jewelry substrate.

In a preferred embodiment, the through hole **18** possesses a substantially circular cross-section having a diameter within the range of approximately 1.0 mm to 3.5 mm, although it will be appreciated that other cross-sectional geometries (e.g., oblong, oval) may be employed without departing from the scope of the invention.

### Hinge Assembly

A second body member **24** is pivotally coupled to the first body member **12** via a hinge assembly **26**. The hinge assembly **26** comprises a barrel portion **28** integrally formed with, or affixed to, the first body member **12**, and a corresponding knuckle portion **30** formed on the second body member **24**. A hinge pin **32** extends through aligned apertures in the barrel portion **28** and knuckle portion **30**, thereby defining a pivot axis **A-A** about which the second body member **24** rotates relative to the first body member **12** between an open configuration and a closed configuration.

The hinge assembly **26** may further include a detent feature or spring-loaded stop (not shown) to bias the second body member **24** toward the closed configuration, reducing the likelihood of inadvertent opening during wear.

### Cavity and Resilient Gripping Element

Formed within the second body member **24** is an internal cavity **34**, sized and configured to receive a resilient gripping element **36** therein. The resilient gripping element **36** may comprise a spring-loaded pawl, a compressible elastomeric pad, a leaf spring, or a coil-biased detent ball, without limitation, provided that the element **36** is capable of exerting a retentive biasing force sufficient to engage a complementary catch surface **38** disposed on the first body member **12**.

In the illustrated embodiment, the resilient gripping element **36** comprises a curved metallic leaf spring **40** having a free end **42** and a fixed end **44**, the fixed end **44** being anchored within the cavity **34** by a retaining pin **46** or adhesive bonding agent. The free end **42** projects partially beyond an opening **48** of the cavity **34**, such that, upon rotation of the second body member **24** into the closed position, the free end **42** engages the catch surface **38** of the first body member **12**, thereby producing a positive mechanical interlock resisting inadvertent separation of the first body member **12** and second body member **24**.

The cavity **34** may further include one or more retention ribs **50** or shoulders formed along its interior surface to prevent dislodgement of the resilient gripping element **36** during repeated actuation cycles, thereby enhancing the operational longevity of the clasp assembly **10**.

In use, a user grasps the first body member **12** and second body member **24**, pivoting the latter about the hinge assembly **26** into the open position, thereby disengaging the resilient gripping element **36** from the catch surface **38**. The clasp assembly **10** is thereafter positioned about a desired attachment point, and the second body member **24** is pivoted back into the closed position, whereupon the free end **42** of the resilient gripping element **36** automatically re-engages the catch surface **38** under spring bias, securing the clasp assembly **10** in the closed configuration until intentionally released by the user.

# Patent Draft: Hinged Friction-Grip Chain Clip

## FIELD OF THE INVENTION

The present invention relates generally to jewelry retention devices, and more particularly to a hinged clip apparatus for frictionally engaging and securing a bracelet or necklace chain to prevent slippage, tangling, or loss during wear or storage.

---

## BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Bracelet and necklace chains are prone to sliding, twisting, or detaching from a desired position, particularly when chains are thin, lightweight, or lack a natural stopping point. Existing solutions often require permanent alteration of the chain, complex clasps, or tools for installation. There exists a need for a simple, reusable, tool-free device capable of securely gripping a chain at a user-selected point without damaging the chain or requiring structural modification.

---

## SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

The present invention provides a two-part clip assembly connected by a hinge, wherein at least one interior surface of the clip incorporates a resilient insert configured to frictionally engage a chain positioned between the two clip bodies when the clip is closed. The hinge permits rotational movement between a first (open) position, in which the chain may be inserted or removed, and a second (closed) position, in which the resilient insert compresses against the chain to produce a retentive frictional force sufficient to prevent unintended displacement of the chain relative to the clip.

---

## DETAILED DESCRIPTION OF THE INVENTION

### 1. General Structure

The clip assembly (100) comprises:

- **A first clip body (110)** and **a second clip body (120)**, each having an interior gripping surface (111, 121) and an exterior surface (112, 122);
- **A hinge (130)** rotatably joining the first clip body (110) to the second clip body (120) along a common edge, permitting angular displacement between an open configuration and a closed configuration;
- **A resilient insert (140)** disposed on at least one interior gripping surface (111 and/or 121), formed from an elastomeric, foam, silicone, rubber, or similarly compressible material;
- **A closure mechanism (150)**, optionally including a latch, magnetic element, snap-fit protrusion, or friction-fit engagement feature, configured to retain the clip bodies (110, 120) in the closed configuration.

### 2. Hinge Configuration

The hinge (130) may be implemented as, without limitation:
- a pin-and-barrel hinge;
- a living hinge integrally molded from a flexible polymer;
- a spring-loaded hinge biasing the clip bodies toward either the open or closed position;
- a torsion-spring hinge providing continuous clamping force against the resilient insert (140).

In a preferred embodiment, the hinge (130) is biased via a torsion spring toward the closed position, such that the resilient insert (140) maintains continuous compressive engagement with the chain absent manual actuation to open the clip.

### 3. Resilient Insert

The resilient insert (140) is affixed to the interior gripping surface (111, 121) via adhesive bonding, mechanical interlock, overmolding, or insertion into a complementary recessed channel (113, 123) formed in the clip body. The insert (140) may comprise:

- closed-cell or open-cell foam;
- silicone rubber;
- thermoplastic elastomer (TPE);
- natural or synthetic rubber;
- a textured or ribbed surface profile to enhance frictional engagement with the chain.

The resilient insert (140) is dimensioned to compress by a predetermined amount upon closure of the clip bodies (110, 120), thereby conforming to the surface contour of the chain and increasing the contact surface area to enhance grip without inducing plastic deformation or damage to the chain links.

In an alternative embodiment, resilient inserts (140a, 140b) are disposed on **both** interior gripping surfaces (111, 121), forming an opposing compressive engagement that fully surrounds a segment of the chain when the clip is closed.

### 4. Closure Mechanism

The closure mechanism (150) may include:

- a snap-fit protrusion (151) on the first clip body (110) engaging a complementary recess (152) on the second clip body (120);
- a magnetic element embedded in each clip body to draw the bodies into the closed position;
- a slide-lock or latch mechanism manually actuated by the user;
- a friction-fit relationship wherein the resilient insert (140) itself provides sufficient closure resistance without additional latching hardware.

### 5. Operation

In use, a user positions a segment of a bracelet or necklace chain (200) between the first clip body (110) and second clip body (120) while the hinge (130) is in the open configuration. The user then rotates the clip bodies about the hinge (130) into the closed configuration, causing the resilient insert (140) to compress against the chain (200). The compressive force generated by the resilient insert (140), in combination with the closure mechanism (150), produces a frictional retention force sufficient to fix the position of the chain (200) relative to the clip assembly (100) during normal use, while remaining manually reversible by reopening the hinge (130).

---

## CLAIMS (Sample Independent Claims)

**Claim 1.**
A clip apparatus for securing a jewelry chain, comprising:
a first clip body having a first interior gripping surface;
a second clip body having a second interior gripping surface;
a hinge rotatably connecting the first clip body to the second clip body between an open configuration and a closed configuration;
a resilient insert disposed on at least one of the first interior gripping surface or the second interior gripping surface;
wherein, in the closed configuration, the resilient insert is configured to compressively and frictionally engage a chain positioned between the first and second interior gripping surfaces, thereby resisting relative movement between the chain and the clip apparatus.

**Claim 2.**
The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the hinge comprises a spring-biased hinge configured to bias the first clip body and the second clip body toward the closed configuration.

**Claim 3.**
The apparatus of claim 1, further comprising a closure mechanism selected from the group consisting of a snap-fit protrusion and recess, a magnetic coupling, and a manually actuated latch, configured to retain the first clip body and second clip body in the closed configuration.

**Claim 4.**
The apparatus of claim 1, wherein the resilient insert comprises a compressible material selected from the group consisting of silicone, foam, rubber, and thermoplastic elastomer.

**Claim 5.**
The apparatus of claim 1, wherein resilient inserts are disposed on both the first interior gripping surface and the second interior gripping surface, forming opposing compressive contact surfaces about the chain when in the closed configuration.

---

## ABSTRACT

A hinged clip apparatus for securing a bracelet or necklace chain includes a first clip body and a second clip body joined by a hinge permitting movement between open and closed configurations. At least one interior gripping surface of the clip bodies includes a resilient insert formed from a compressible material such as silicone, foam, or rubber. When the clip is closed about a segment of chain, the resilient insert compresses against the chain, generating a frictional retention force sufficient to prevent unwanted sliding or displacement of the chain while remaining manually releasable by reopening the hinge.

# Patent Abstract

**Wearable Jewelry Clip with Resilient Securing Mechanism**

A wearable jewelry clip apparatus configured to releasably secure the device to an elongated member, such as a chain, cord, ribbon, or similar flexible article. The clip comprises a body defining an internal channel sized to receive the elongated member, and a closure mechanism operable between an open configuration for receiving or releasing the member and a closed configuration for retaining the member within the channel.

The apparatus further includes a resilient biasing element, such as a coil spring, leaf spring, or spring-loaded hinge, disposed within or coupled to the clip body. The resilient element applies a continuous inward or clamping force against the closure mechanism, urging it toward the closed configuration and thereby maintaining frictional or compressive engagement with the elongated member once inserted. This spring-biased arrangement allows the clip to be manually opened against the resilient force to accept the elongated member, and automatically returns to a secured, closed position upon release, eliminating the need for separate locking mechanisms, adhesives, or fasteners.

The clip body may be fabricated from metal, alloy, or rigid polymer and may incorporate decorative elements, gemstones, or ornamental finishes on an exterior surface, enabling the device to function simultaneously as a functional securing mechanism and a piece of wearable jewelry. The design permits repeated attachment and removal without degradation of the resilient element's biasing force, and accommodates elongated members of varying diameters within a defined range through the inherent flexibility of the spring mechanism.

In various embodiments, the clip may be configured for attachment to necklaces, bracelets, eyeglass chains, lanyards, or similar items, and may include an additional attachment point, such as a loop or ring, for securing supplementary ornamental or functional accessories to the clip itself.

# TECHNICAL DISCLOSURE

## CLASP ASSEMBLY WITH HINGED DUAL-BODY CONSTRUCTION AND RESILIENT THROUGH-CAVITY GRIPPING ELEMENT

---

### [0001] FIELD OF THE INVENTION

This disclosure relates generally to fastening devices, and more particularly to a two-part clasp assembly employing a hinge connection and a resilient gripping element that is partially housed within an internal cavity of one clasp part and partially exposed through a through hole to engage and releasably retain the mating clasp part. The invention is applicable to jewelry (necklaces, bracelets), watch bands, belts, straps, harnesses, luggage fittings, and similar articles requiring a secure, repeatably operable closure.

---

### [0002] BACKGROUND OF THE INVENTION

Conventional clasps rely on one or more of the following retention strategies: (a) friction fit between mating surfaces, (b) a separate spring-loaded pin or ball detent housed entirely within one body, or (c) a simple hook-and-eye arrangement lacking positive mechanical locking. Friction-only designs loosen with wear and are prone to inadvertent opening. Fully enclosed spring-and-pin mechanisms often require multiple discrete parts (springs, pins, retaining caps), increasing manufacturing complexity, part count, and assembly cost, while also creating multiple failure points.

[0003] There remains a need for a clasp construction that (i) uses a reduced part count, (ii) provides positive, tactile, repeatable locking engagement, (iii) is resistant to unintentional release under incidental loading, and (iv) can be actuated with one hand without tools.

---

### [0004] SUMMARY OF THE INVENTION

[0005] The present invention provides a clasp assembly comprising a first part and a second part joined by a hinge such that the second part is movable relative to the first part between an open position and a closed position. The first part defines an internal cavity and a through hole that places the cavity in communication with the exterior of the first part. A resilient element is disposed partly within the cavity and partly outside the cavity, the two regions being continuous portions of a single resilient body that passes through the through hole.

[0006] The portion of the resilient element residing inside the cavity ("inner portion") is retained against, or anchored to, an interior wall of the first part and supplies a restoring/biasing force. The portion of the resilient element residing outside the cavity ("outer portion") projects through the through hole and presents a gripping surface. When the second part is rotated about the hinge into the closed position, a mating engagement feature on the second part (e.g., a pin, tab, ridge, or detent) contacts the outer portion of the resilient element, causing the outer portion to elastically deflect and then resiliently close around, or seat against, the engagement feature, thereby producing a positive, releasable, snap-fit lock. Manual inward displacement of the outer portion (directly, or via a release surface on the second part) disengages the grip and permits the second part to be pivoted back to the open position.

[0007] Because the inner and outer portions are regions of one continuous resilient body rather than separate components, the assembly achieves gripping/locking functionality, spring biasing, and (optionally) a tactile "click" feedback with a minimum of discrete parts.

---
